PERFORMANCE ENGINEER, KERNELS

Part of Sarvam's Performance Engineering team. We are hiring two specialized performance roles - Kernels (this posting) and Inference (companion posting). They are a vertical stack: the kernels team authors the µs-level GPU code, and the inference team integrates it into a running serving stack and owns the system-level numbers. If your depth genuinely spans both, apply to either and tell us - but most candidates are strongest in one, and we hire for that depth.



Location: [Bengaluru / Chennai / Hybrid / On-site]  ·  Team: Performance Engineering  ·  Level: Senior




ABOUT THE TEAM

Sarvam serves multiple model families - small and large LLMs, Mixture-of-Experts, streaming Indic ASR, and multimodal - across a multi-node, multi-tenant fleet on H100 / H200 / B200. The Performance Engineering team owns the numbers the rest of the company plans against: how fast we serve, how much it costs, and how much we get out of every GPU. This team works at the intersection of the serving runtime, the kernel layer, and the SRE org that keeps the fleet alive.



ABOUT THE ROLE

You will own the kernel layer. Where stock libraries - cuBLAS, cuDNN, FlashAttention, out-of-the-box Triton - leave performance on the table, you will author the custom CUDA, DSL-based, and PTX kernels that close the gap.



This is a hard, narrow, high-leverage role. We hire engineers who have shipped kernels that beat published baselines on real workloads, not engineers who have used kernels. When your code lands, production p99 moves, and you own the explanation of why.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years in ML systems, with 2+ years authoring production CUDA kernels. You have a kernel in production that beat the prior baseline by a measurable margin.

 - CUDA at kernel-authoring level: thread-block sizing, shared-memory layout, warp primitives, async copies (cp.async, TMA), and MMA selection.

 - CUTLASS / CuTe DSL at a modify-and-extend level, with comfort in the layout algebra.

 - PTX at a debug-and-modify level - you have inserted hand-written PTX where the compiler missed.

 - Nsight Compute and Systems fluency: you read a roofline plot and propose the fix.

 - Attention kernels: you have authored or modified at least one (FlashAttention-family, paged, MLA, sliding-window, or sparse).

 - Multi-architecture awareness: what changes from Hopper to Blackwell (TMA, WGMMA, tcgen05).



STRONG PLUSES

 - Communication kernels - NCCL / NVSHMEM authoring, custom collectives, expert-parallel dispatch (DeepEP-style), AFD bipartite comms (StepMesh-style), KV transfer (DualPath / Mooncake). Strongly desired; dedicated comms-specialist headcount is expected later.

 - Open-source kernel contributions - FlashAttention, CUTLASS examples, vLLM / SGLang kernels, DeepEP, Mooncake, or non-trivial Triton work. For this role, the GitHub filter is the highest-yield signal.

 - tcgen05, TMA, CTA-cluster launch and distributed shared memory, async pipelining, and the FP4/microscaling paths

 - Grace-side host-path optimization on GH200 / GB200.

title: Deployment Strategist
description:
India's largest banks, insurers, digital natives and government departments are not short of AI pilots. They are short of AI in production.

WHO YOU ARE

title: Agent Engineer
description:
The distance between an AI system that works and one that millions of people rely on every day is where the real engineering lives. Crossing it is what Agent Engineers at Sarvam do.

The agents you build go into live operation at India's largest banks, insurers, NBFCs and government departments, and at some of the country's fastest-growing companies, handling millions of real interactions, measured against outcomes the customer wants to drive.

The hard part is not the first version. It is everything after: mapping the full space of what an agent has to handle so the scenarios that matter are covered by design rather than discovered in production, engineering for the failure modes instead of the happy path, and building the evals and instrumentation that make quality measurable, so drift surfaces in the data rather than in a customer escalation.

We treat agents as code. Not prompts someone tweaks in a console, but engineered artifacts: versioned, reviewed, and held to a regression suite, where you can reason about what a change will do and roll it back if you are wrong. Anyone who has watched an AI system quietly decay because nobody could tell which change broke it understands why this matters.

And then doing it again for the next customer, faster, because you built the first one to be repeatable.


ABOUT SARVAM

Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.


WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU

Production, at real scale

Not prototypes, not demos. Systems in live operation at some of India's largest institutions, carrying real volume, measured against outcomes the customer has signed up to. You will see the consequences of your engineering decisions within days.

You work at the source

Sarvam builds the whole stack: the foundational models, the infrastructure they run on, and the products on top of them. When a deployment needs something that does not exist yet, whether that is model behaviour, an infrastructure capability or a product change, you are not filing a ticket with a vendor and waiting on a roadmap. You are in a room with the people who built it. Anyone who has delivered AI on top of someone else's black box knows how much difference that makes.

A genuinely broad surface

Sarvam's products span conversational AI, agentic workflows, intelligent document processing, and content, including dubbing and document translation. You will own a motion and go deep in it, and the depth you build travels well as products mature and new ones ship.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build production agents on the Sarvam stack: prompts, system design, workflows, tool integrations, and evals.

 - Map the space the agent has to cover. Work out the scenarios that matter, how each should be handled, and where the edges are, so coverage is designed rather than discovered later.

 - Build the proof of concept when a customer wants to see it work before committing at scale, and get to a convincing result fast.

The monogram is a gateway that emerges — layered circles resolving out of mandala geometry into a single threshold form. Both are currently being made mostly in stills.

We want the person who resolves that. Not someone to animate a logo once for a launch, but someone who decides how this brand behaves — how it enters, how it responds, how a gradient moves without becoming wallpaper — and then builds that language across films, web and product.

It’s a rare brief: a real identity with real motion logic baked into it, and nobody has run at it yet.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Define the motion language, not just the motion. Timing, easing, entrances, transitions, how the monogram behaves and how the gradient travels — documented and reusable, so the next fifty assets don’t start from zero.

 - Make the films. Model launches, product announcements, research drops, event opens, brand pieces. Concept, board, animate, edit, sound, deliver — you’ll own the shot end to end.

 - Make the product move too. Web animation, scroll behaviour, UI micro-interactions, demo and walkthrough videos. This is the half of the role that keeps the other half honest: motion that ships inside a live surface has constraints a film doesn’t.

 - Hand off cleanly to engineering. Lottie, Rive, sprite sequences, or a spec an engineer can actually build from. Work that dies in After Effects doesn’t count.

 - Solve the hard one: visualising speech. Our products are conversational — voice agents across 11 Indian languages, code-switching mid-sentence. Showing listening, thinking, speaking and switching, without falling back on a generic waveform, is the most interesting motion problem in the building.

 - Use AI properly in the pipeline. Generative video, boards and previz, roto, upscaling, variation. You should already be doing this, with a clear sense of where it saves a week and where it costs you the shot.

 - Work across the whole company. Design, marketing, product, research, founders. Rough briefs, hard launch dates, and work that still holds up at the end of it.
   
   


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years in motion design, in-house or at a studio, with a reel that shows both narrative work and work that shipped inside a product or website.

title: Software Development Engineer - Tejas
description:
Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends.

Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. The memory side lets agents remember what they learn over time, about individual users, about teams, and across the organisation. We want both to keep improving as they are used.

Knowledge and memory for agents is a rapidly evolving field. We want to build at the frontier of it, and to show with measurable results that our approach does better than traditional ones.



ABOUT SARVAM

Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.



WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU

You will join a small team and own large parts of the platform. The work is driven by real customer deployments, so what you build gets used quickly and you see what works and what does not. You will also work closely with the teams building Sarvam's models, document AI and inference, which makes it much easier to solve problems that cut across the stack.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and run the ingestion pipeline that parses, extracts and indexes large volumes of documents, and keep it reliable when files are messy and external services fail.

 - Connect to databases and enterprise systems so agents can work with structured records as well as documents.

 - Design how enterprise data is modelled, including the ontology, matching the same entity across sources, and tracing every value back to where it came from.

 - Build the retrieval tools agents call, with search, filters and citations, and make them fast and cheap enough for agents to use heavily.

 - Build memory for agents at the level of a user, a team and the whole organisation: how it is written, stored, retrieved and kept accurate over time.

 - Run evals, find where answers go wrong, and keep iterating until quality improves.

 - Work with product and forward-deployed engineers to turn what one customer needs into something the platform does for every customer.

 - Write design docs and keep decisions documented.

Our production stack is Go, with Temporal, OpenSearch and Postgres.



WHO YOU ARE

We are hiring at 3 to 5 years of experience.

 - You have built and run backend or data systems in production, and you have fixed them when they broke.

 - You are strong in at least one backend language. Our core is in Go, so Go experience is a plus, and you should be happy to work in it every day.

 - You have good fundamentals in data modelling and PostgreSQL.

 - You have worked on long-running pipelines and know how to make them safe to retry and recover.

 - You have worked on search or retrieval and know how to debug why the right result did not come back.

 - You use AI coding tools every day and have a good sense of where they help and where they don't.

 - You care about measuring quality, and you are comfortable building the evals to do it.


BONUS POINTS

 - Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, entity resolution or structured extraction.

 - Experience building memory for agents or LLM applications.

 - Document processing, such as OCR, layout or table extraction.

 - Connectors or change data capture for ERP, CRM or other enterprise systems.

 - Building on MCP, or serving LLMs and embedding models in production.

 - On-prem or air-gapped deployments.

 - Experience at an early- or growth-stage startup.

title: Marketing internship (brand & communication)
description:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India, a full-stack sovereign AI platform spanning research, models, infrastructure, and applications, with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. We partner with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.



About the Role

We are looking for a sharp, high-ownership Marketing Intern to act as the primary story-builder and content engine across Sarvam’s marketing channels.

This is not a passive internship focused on surface-level social updates. You will translate complex frontier AI capabilities like our Vision APIs, Document Intelligence models, and voice platforms into crisp, high-impact stories, viral launch threads, and sharp enterprise collateral. You will sit at the intersection of product, creative execution, and creator operations, helping shape how Sarvam communicates its sovereign AI vision to technical builders, enterprise buyers, and the broader ecosystem.



What You'll Do

Customer Stories & Launch Comms

 - Transform technical milestones into narratives: Turn enterprise customer deployments into compelling case studies and written success stories.

 - Drive product launch comms: Draft multi-channel launch content—from sharp X/LinkedIn feature threads to enterprise mailers for prospects and existing clients.

 - Simplify the complex: Translate technical AI concepts into clear, punchy prose without losing accuracy or depth.

Social Content & Video Operations

 - Drive video execution: Write scripts for explainer videos and product walkthroughs; coordinate shoots and post-production workflows.

 - Manage multi-platform publishing: Oversee daily social presence across X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube, ensuring high content velocity and visual quality.

Creator & Influencer Operations

 - Manage creator partnerships: Source, pitch, and recruit relevant tech creators, developer voices, and industry influencers.

 - Execute campaign logistics: Draft campaign briefs, align timelines, and track deliverables from initial outreach to final publish.



What We're Looking For

 - Editorial precision: Exceptional written English skills with an instinct for tone, structure, and clarity across social, email, and long-form formats.

 - Technical translation capability: Comfortable diving into technical platforms, developer dashboards, or AI research to write simple, accurate marketing copy.

 - AI-first workflow: Habitual use of AI tools for rapid research, content structuring, and drafting.

 - Platform fluency: Deep, native understanding of content formats, algorithms, and tone across X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube.

 - Execution & ownership: Uncompromising attention to detail, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to drive multiple deadlines without hand-holding.



Bonus Points

 - Hands-on experience with video editing tools or basic script-to-edit workflows.

 - Familiarity with design tools (Canva, Figma) to quickly mock up assets or social creatives.

 - Prior experience managing creator outreach, influencer pipelines, or talent operations.

 - Vernacular fluency in Hindi or a regional Indian language.

 - Foundational understanding of SEO best practices for written content.
   
   

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems at the frontier of AI with population-scale impact. You'll work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar. High ownership and high impact from day one, AI-first in everything we do, on problems that could change how an entire country works and communicates.

title: Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About the team

Sarvam builds Indic-language AI used at population scale. The CPU Infrastructure team runs everything outside the GPU fleet: Kubernetes across Azure, AWS, GCP and Indian sovereign clouds, the network between them, Cloudflare, identity, secrets, observability, cost and the delivery pipeline every product ships through.

The team builds and runs what it builds. Engineers own real systems end to end, and every repeated piece of manual work is a candidate for automation. As an AI company, we are building AI agents into our own operations, to plan and review infrastructure changes, triage alerts and handle routine issues, with engineers setting the guardrails.

About the role

You keep the infrastructure behind Sarvam’s products running. You handle day-to-day operations — deployments, provisioning, access, incidents and cost questions — and you are expected to automate that work away.

We hire for one instinct above everything else: you notice something done by hand every day, ask why it can’t run itself, and build the thing that removes it — a script, a pipeline step, a bot, a small Kubernetes operator, or an AI agent that does the work. Operations is a large part of this role, and it is where you find what is worth automating.

As you automate your own toil away, more of your time goes into platform and automation work.

Products you may work on

Sarvam builds across a broad range of AI products: voice agents, coding agents, coworker agents, dubbing, our API platform, and the real-time voice and WebRTC infrastructure underneath them, among many others. You will work on the infrastructure behind them.

Responsibilities

• Own infrastructure operations across Sarvam’s products: deployments, provisioning requests, access, environment issues, cost questions

• Respond to incidents, write the runbook or postmortem afterwards, and fix the cause

• Automate repeated work: turn manual steps into pipeline jobs, Terraform modules, templates or self-service for product teams

• Build AI-assisted automations: agents that triage alerts, summarise incidents, review routine changes or answer product teams’ infrastructure questions, with a human approving anything risky

• Security basics: keep images and dependencies patched, rotate credentials, keep secrets out of code, fix security findings

• Reliability basics: keep dashboards and alerts accurate, track SLOs and cost, delete noisy alerts

• Take part in on-call

Requirements

• 2–5 years in DevOps, SRE, infrastructure or backend engineering

• Has built infrastructure outside a ticket: a homelab, an open-source contribution, a side project, or an internal tool nobody asked for — and can show the code (GitHub, a blog post or a demo)

• Comfortable on the Linux command line: processes, networking basics, logs, systemd

• Working knowledge of Docker and Kubernetes; has deployed and debugged something running on a cluster

• Scripting in Python, Go or Bash

• Basic Git and CI/CD experience

• Has spotted a repeated manual task — a daily review, a recurring fix, a routine request — and built something that removed it: a script, a CI job, a bot or a Kubernetes operator. You can walk us through what you noticed, why it mattered, what you built and what it saved

• Has used LLMs or AI agents to automate real work, not only for writing code

• Fixes causes rather than the same symptom twice; asks “why is this manual?” before doing it again

• Curious, takes ownership, wants to grow into platform engineering

• Nice to have: Terraform, a public cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP), Prometheus / Grafana, exposure to SIP, WebRTC or real-time media, any cloud or Kubernetes certification

title: SDE3, Infrastructure Security Engineer (DevSecOps)
description:
About the team

Sarvam builds Indic-language AI used at population scale. The CPU Infrastructure team runs everything outside the GPU fleet: Kubernetes across Azure, AWS, GCP and Indian sovereign clouds, the network between them, Cloudflare, identity, secrets, observability, cost and the delivery pipeline every product ships through.

The team builds and runs what it builds. Engineers own real systems end to end, and every repeated piece of manual work is a candidate for automation. As an AI company, we are building AI agents into our own operations, to plan and review infrastructure changes, triage alerts and handle routine issues, with engineers setting the guardrails.

About the role

You are an infrastructure engineer whose first instinct is security, and who builds rather than only operates. You have worked on banking, fintech, payments or similarly regulated products, where a misconfiguration is an incident and an audit is routine. Here you set what “secure” means across Sarvam’s infrastructure and build the automation that enforces it, so security is a property of the pipeline rather than a review step. You work closely with the compliance team.

This is a hands-on role: most of your time goes into building, and you guide engineering teams across Sarvam on security — setting standards, reviewing security-relevant work and mentoring engineers.

Responsibilities

• Define and enforce security baselines for Kubernetes, cloud accounts, container images and CI/CD across all clouds

• Write the policy gates in the delivery pipeline (OPA / Conftest, Kyverno or equivalent): network exposure, IAM, image provenance, secrets, data residency

• Own secrets and workload identity: Vault or cloud-native equivalents, rotation, short-lived and scoped credentials, no long-lived keys

• Build detection and response: runtime security (Falco / Tetragon or equivalent), log-based detections, alerting and playbooks

• Run the finding-to-fix loop for security findings: triage, assign, fix, add a detection, retest

• Use LLMs and AI agents in security work: triaging findings, reviewing infrastructure changes, tuning detections, drafting incident timelines — and secure the agents themselves with scoped, short-lived permissions and audit trails

• Harden the supply chain: image signing and scanning, dependency policy, SBOMs

• Automate compliance evidence (CERT-In, ISO 27001, SOC 2, DPDP) together with the compliance team

• Set the security standards other engineers follow and review security-relevant changes

• Take part in on-call and lead security incidents

Requirements

• 5–9 years in DevOps, platform or security engineering, with at least 2 in a bank, fintech, payments company or other regulated environment

• Strong Kubernetes and Linux fundamentals; has run production clusters on at least one major cloud

• Hands-on with Terraform / OpenTofu and GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)

• Has built security automation, not only operated tools: policy-as-code, secrets rotation, CI/CD security gates or detection pipelines

• Working knowledge of IAM, network security, TLS and secrets management across clouds

• Scripting and tooling in Python or Go

• Has been through security audits and knows what evidence auditors need

• Has built or used AI-based automation in infrastructure or security work, and understands the risks of AI agents: prompt injection, over-broad permissions, unreviewed actions

• Nice to have: Vault, SPIFFE / SPIRE, Falco or Tetragon, Cloudflare WAF, incident response lead experience, multi-cloud experience
